title: A finite unramified morphism with one purely inseparable fibre point is locally a closed immersion
statement: Let $\pi:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s\in S$, and let $x\in X$ be the unique point of the underlying topological fibre $\pi^{-1}(s)$, equivalently the unique point of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], and that the residue-field extension $\kappa(s)\subseteq\kappa(x)$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restricted morphism $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. (Stacks Project, Tag [04DG].)
